ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer for a safety review of the driver's conduct; do not auto-execute any refund. Reviewer should confirm the trip path (no off-route segment, F1), the rider's mid-ride exit request [F3] and the driver's message [F4], and decide whether the driver's conduct violates Ryde's code of conduct.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a safety dispute filed by the rider: the rider says the driver threatened to lock her in when she asked to get out [case][F3]. The scope screen in SAFE-1 requires the judge to read the chat, the complaint and the driver's statement for threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegations and, if any is found, to send the case to a human instead of ruling [SAFE-1]. The complaint and the two-message chat amount to that escalation trigger, so no automatic refund or no-action ruling is available on this record.

Reading the words in context: at 17:09 the rider asked the car to stop so she could get out [F3]; one minute later the driver wrote "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4]. That is a statement of control over whether the rider could leave the vehicle, made to a rider who was asking to exit mid-ride — I read it as at least an intimidation / abuse-of-a-rider concern under SAFE-1, not a route argument. The driver's later written statement says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and that he told her to sit down "for her own safety" [F6], and this does not remove the concern: the written words themselves ("or I lock the doors") are what the rider experienced as a threat [F4][F6].

The rider's stated feeling of being unsafe for the remainder of the ride [case] is a safety-harm allegation about an event during the trip [F2], for which Ryde's code of conduct bars abuse of any kind and threats and intimidation, and Ryde's safety path is a human review rather than an automated fare decision [SAFE-1]. That path is enough for this case: escal = true, amount = null (escalate carries no amount) [SAFE-1]. The trace marks the safety screen settled, so the only permissible outcome is escalate [SAFE-1].

Evidence status: the record I need to escalate is complete — both chat messages are timestamped and the record is whole [F5], the trip timing and path are recorded [F1][F2], and the driver gave a statement [F6]. Nothing in the ruling turns on the missing route-deviation record: the path deviates -0.1 km from the optimal route (-0%) [F1], i.e. there is no off-route segment fact, so route-deviation review is moot here [RD-1]. Evidence is therefore sufficient for the escalation. Because the case is a safety escalation, no refund amount is computed and no account action is attached by this ruling; the reviewer decides what, if any, conduct action follows [SAFE-1].

For completeness on the fare: this was a fixed-fare RydeX trip charged $32.86, and with no off-route segment [F1] there is no unexempted extra mileage and no disclosed add-on to refund [RD-2]. I note only that the case record is insufficient to decide any fare question, so the escalation leaves the charge as it stands [RD-2].

Recommended action: hand the case to a human safety reviewer to assess the driver's mid-ride conduct and decide follow-up; no automated refund or fee action [SAFE-1][RD-2].
